meta.outcomeNote: Weights are set by the effect on heat-emergency incidence, which replaced the Heat Vulnerability Index as the target: HVI varied almost entirely between neighbourhoods rather than between cells, while heat emergencies retain 39% of their variance within a neighbourhood. Surface temperature and the vulnerability index are reported alongside as mediators on the pathway.
meta.scale: standardised (SD of outcome per SD of indicator)
meta.weightRule: magnitude = |effect| x reliability x tierFactor, where reliability = theta^2/(theta^2+se^2) and tierFactor encodes FCI's identification verdict; variable weight = magnitude / category mean magnitude, then blended back toward the balanced weight of 1 in proportion to (1 - reliability x tierFactor); category weight is the same rule applied to category totals; both clipped to the app slider range [0, 2]
meta.shrinkageRationale: A weight is allowed to travel from the balanced default only when the estimate is both precise and identified. Precision is measured by reliability; identification by FCI, which tests pair by pair whether an unmeasured common cause is required. Most indicators here are not identified at the data's true spatial resolution, so most weights stay near 1 -- that is the finding, not a failure of the method.

tiers.confounded: FCI finds an unmeasured common cause
tiers.undetected: no effect detectable at this resolution

meta.inference: standard errors clustered on neighbourhood tabulation areas; cross-fitting folds grouped by the same clusters
meta.caveat: Indicators marked constructOverlap contribute to the published HVI formula, so part of their estimated effect is definitional rather than causal.

shapley.quantity: Shapley decomposition of explained variance in heat-emergency incidence across the fitted SCM
shapley.weightRule: The Shapley value is the weight. One slider per indicator holds its shapley_share directly; there is no category multiplier and no rescaling. A category's weight is the sum of the shares of its live indicators (share > 0 and a reading in this cell) and its reading is the plain, unweighted mean of their directed percentiles, so priority = sum over categories of (summed share x mean percentile), gated on population. Shares sum to 1 across the full indicator set, so a fully-read cell lands on 0-100 with no normalising constant; the sum is deliberately not renormalised, so a cell with missing categories scores lower.
shapley.rationale: Shapley shares are attributions, not effect estimates, so they are used at face value rather than shrunk toward 1 or renormalised against a category mean. Weighting happens once, at the category level: an indicator's share sets how much its group counts, and inside the group every live indicator counts the same. That keeps the control surface honest -- the number on the slider is the quantity the score uses, not a display artefact -- and it makes a zeroed slider mean what it looks like it means, since a share of zero drops the indicator out of its category's mean as well as out of its weight.
shapley.note: 18 of 43 indicators receive a Shapley share of zero: their marginal contribution to explained variance was non-positive across every coalition ordering sampled. They carry no weight in the priority score. A zero weight means the indicator earned no attribution here, not that it is causally irrelevant.
shapley.caveat: Attribution is estimated from 6 point fits and 16 bootstrap replicates, so shares under about 1% are not separable from one another and most per-indicator intervals span zero. Read the ordering at the top of the table and the category totals; do not read fine distinctions in the tail.
shapley.liveWeights: The app treats these shares as defaults. Users move them, and the priority score, the category readouts and the intervention ranking all follow the live values.
